column1: # Every answer found in which a Chinese government spokesperson was asked about Nvidia chips, about American chips or about the sale of chips to China: 31 exchanges, made on Nov 25, 2026, one of them added on Nov 26, 2026. The rule: an exchange is counted when the question's own words name Nvidia or one of its chips, an American chip, or chips or semiconductors with their export to, sale in or purchase by China; a question on export controls, tariffs or technology that names no chip is not counted, nor one on chip-making equipment, on chips made in China or on rare earths, nor an answer that brings up chips where the question did not. Three of the commerce ministry's rows are counted on a wider reading of that rule: May 22, 2025 (American export controls on AI chips, with no destination named in the question), May 29, 2025 (American chip export controls, as the question names them, with no destination named) and Jul 31, 2025 (high-end chips as one subject of the two countries' trade talks). Foreign ministry (20): all 411 transcripts of its regular press conferences from December 2024 to Sept 13, 2026 were read by a search program, and the pages that matched its chip words were read twice, the second time by this rule, by three readers who were not told the table's rows and who found all 18 exchanges of the first reading and two more. Commerce ministry (11): 31 regular briefings were read, and a second search read its briefings of 2025 and 2026 at their dated addresses (six of the eleven rows); one more exchange, of May 29, 2025, was found on Nov 26, 2026 among the saved pages and is read in the ministry's English transcript; its written answers have no full list and were found by search only, so the commerce rows are not a census. Columns: date; ministry; spokesperson; who asked; the question's words in Chinese as the page gives them, or its gist; the class of the answer; the answer's words in Chinese, each checked against the saved copy by script; the saved id; whether the project's record already held the exchange. Two exchanges that meet the rule but do not bear on Chinese policy toward these chips are left out (Jun 19 and Aug 7, 2025). For Sept 14 to Nov 24, 2026 see section 8 of OFFICIAL_RECORD.md. No answer in the table confirms or denies a restriction, an instruction or an approval.
